purpose: Execute a safe, bounded JSON query over normalized canonical LIVE data.
parameters:
``request`` must explicitly include supported ``(schema_version, language_version)``
pair (``('1.0', '1.0')`` for exact legacy or ``('1.1', '1.1')`` for progressive
disclosure), ``root``, ``filters`` and ``select``. It may include ``limit``
(default 20, maximum 200) and in 1.1 optional ``evidence_limit`` (default 3,
``None`` for full selected nested evidence, ``0`` for counts only). Cross-version
pairs fail closed. Filters are a flat AND and use only the operators declared for
each field by ``describe_canonical_state``. Empty ``filters`` matches all
records; empty ``select`` returns every selectable field. Results always report
``total_matches``, ``returned``, ``limit`` and ``truncated``.

In language 1.1, emitted ``imports`` and ``consumers`` are bounded by
``evidence_limit`` and accompanied by ``imports_truncated`` or
``consumers_truncated`` metadata. Companion truncation fields exist in schema 1.1
but are not independently selectable (explicit selection returns
``field_not_selectable``). When nested evidence is truncated, a response-level
``expand`` descriptor with ``retry_with_full_evidence`` is emitted. Pass
``evidence_limit=None`` for selected-scope lossless nested retrieval; full-root
retrieval remains bounded by ``max_limit=200`` without continuation tokens.
errors:
The executor first converts LIVE state to read-only JSON-safe records. It
never uses ``eval``, accepts no Python expressions, exposes no arbitrary
attributes and omits local absolute paths. Artifacts preserve the
distinction between confirmed zero consumers and unavailable consumption
data via ``consumer_data_available`` plus nullable consumer fields.
Structural errors return one deterministic error with ``code``, ``path``
and repair details.
usage_notes:
LLM use: discover the contract first via ``describe_canonical_state(schema_version='1.1', language_version='1.1')``,
request the smallest useful field selection, and narrow filters when ``truncated`` is
true. Use ``evidence_limit=None`` only when complete nested evidence is required.
